sections.title: Planning a Network Graphics Meeting
sections.content:
Project MAC planned a network graphics meeting for April and wanted to use part of the February Network Working Group meeting in Urbana to discuss its length, format, structure, and content. The note says this informal discussion could begin considering topics for the larger meeting.

The proposed April meeting would last two full days. Each represented organization was expected to present one or more working papers, with notes and an oral presentation. The bulk of the meeting would be prepared presentations followed by discussion; about three hours at the end of the second day were reserved for open discussion and planning.
sections.plainLanguage: Project MAC proposed a two-day meeting about network graphics in April. It wanted the February meeting in Urbana to help decide what the April event should cover.

sections.title: Suggested Topics for the Meeting
sections.content:
The note suggests four kinds of contributions: descriptions of current or planned graphical facilities connected to the network; descriptions of facilities people would like the network to support; proposals for network graphics protocols, including preliminary proposals intended to raise issues; and accounts of experience, problems, solutions, and unanswered questions.

Organizations were asked to prepare working papers on one or more of these topics. The RFC leaves the choice of authors and division of work to each organization.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants could describe graphics facilities, propose what the network should support, suggest protocols, or share problems and solutions from their work.

sections.title: How Participants Could Contribute
sections.content:
Participants could send suggestions to someone from their site attending the Urbana meeting or contact Fran Yost or A. Vezza at Project MAC. The note asks each organization to bring to the February meeting a list of people actively working on graphics facilities connected to or planned for the network.

The stated aim was to leave the Urbana meeting with a firm concept of the April network graphics meeting. The RFC is a request for planning input, not a report on the later meeting.
sections.plainLanguage: Organizations were asked to bring a list of their graphics participants and share suggestions before or during the Urbana meeting. The goal was to settle the plan for April.
